title: Policy drift caused cross-region reroute echoes and variant misapply
creator: Aisha Narang
description: Customer-facing latency and error spike caused by routing policy drift that triggered cross-region reroutes to an incompatible quantized model variant. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At ~2025-02-11 22:14 UTC a subset of requests for hosted customers experienced elevated 5xx rates and 5x latency for ~37 minutes. The root trigger was a config push that introduced a drift between the routing policy cache and the variant compatibility table; stale policy entries caused repeated reroutes across regions and selection of a quantized variant that lacked a compatible kernel path on the serving fleet, resulting in retries and expensive fallbacks.
timeline: 2025-02-11 21:58 UTC - Config push deploy (policy-mgmt v3.14) started; included new soft-rollout rules for tiered latency routing.
2025-02-11 22:05 UTC - Telemetry alerts: per-route p95 latency rising to 600ms (baseline 90ms) for model redwood-chat-11b-quant on eu-west-1.
2025-02-11 22:14 UTC - Error budget alert: increased 5xx for multiple customers; on-call paged.

2025-02-11 22:18 UTC - Initial investigation: smart-routing logs show repeated reroute decisions for same request IDs with alternating region headers (eu-west-1 <-> us-east-1) and TTL refreshes on routing-header.
2025-02-11 22:24 UTC - Hot mitigation: reverted policy-mgmt v3.14 config to previous stable (v3.13); temporarily pinned region affinity for affected routes.
2025-02-11 22:37 UTC - Error rates and latency returned to baseline after mitigation steps; incident declared resolved at 22:45 UTC after 30m of healthy telemetry.
2025-02-12 09:00 UTC - Post-incident triage meeting; gather logs, dump policy cache states, and kick off root cause analysis.
2025-02-12 14:30 UTC - Root cause hypothesis validated: policy cache mutation + TTL misalignment + stale variant compatibility table entry.
impact_summary: ~4200 requests (0.03% of baseline) experienced elevated latency or 5xx. Three self-serve customers reported elevated error rates and one customer experienced a degraded SLO for 45 minutes. No data plane secrets or PII exposure.
root_cause: A policy push introduced a rule that used an outdated variant selector expression. The routing controller updated policy cache entries but due to a race in the policy-diff apply path one node retained an older routing header TTL value. The header TTL mismatch caused clients to be sticky to regions while the controller simultaneously retried routing decisions; combined with the stale variant compatibility table (not refreshed after a model onboarding change), the controller selected a quantized variant that lacked a supported kernel on the receiving node, causing fallbacks to a slower CPU path and repeated reroutes.
detection: Detected via per-route latency and 5xx alerts, augmented by new smart-routing telemetry that logs variant resolution reasons. Investigation used request-ID trace correlation and policy cache dump across a 6-node serving ring to identify TTL skew.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back policy-mgmt config to v3.13, pinned region affinity for affected routes, and disabled the new variant selector expression. Kicked a cache invalidation job to unify the variant compatibility table across control-plane replicas.
long_term_mitigation: 1) Add atomic policy-diff apply with quorum acknowledgement to prevent partial rollouts. 2) Enforce explicit TTL propagation checks and add a canary verification for routing header coherence. 3) Add compatibility gating: model onboarding must publish compatibility signatures that the routing controller validates before selecting a variant. 4) Add a circuit breaker in smart-routing to avoid cross-region retries beyond 2 hops.
action_items: Benji Cole - Implement policy-diff quorum apply and server-side validation (due 2025-03-07)
Mei Tanaka - Add routing-header TTL coherence checks and alerting (due 2025-02-28)
Ravi Patel - Implement model compatibility signature validation in variant resolver (due 2025-03-14)
Lina Gomez - Add routing circuit-breaker to prevent >2 cross-region reroute hops and add synthetic tests (due 2025-03-01)
Aisha Narang - Update runbook for cross-region reroute incidents and add checklist for hot rollback (due 2025-02-20)
Infra Team - Add a background job to refresh variant compatibility table every 5 minutes with exponential backoff on failures (owner: infra-team, due 2025-03-10)
DevOps - Create a dashboard widget showing per-route variant-resolution mismatches and TTL skew (due 2025-02-25)
customer_communication: 2025-02-12 - Sent incident summary to affected customers with mitigation steps and timeline; offered credit for downtime per SLA.
2025-02-17 - Follow-up email with planned mitigations and timeline for fixes; invited customers to a technical review meeting.
